claim: The CLI sample creates isolated output with branches, tags, a rendered pull-request record, real SQLite mappings and audit events, and a committed JSON archive without reading configuration or token values.
where: landing sample panel, demo page, README
sandbox: fresh CLI process with canary tokens and an invalid configuration in its working directory; inspect only its new operating-system temporary directory

claim: The browser sample uses demo-prefixed storage; reset replaces only its demo session and Start for real discards it without changing non-demo storage.
where: landing demo banner, demo page, privacy page
sandbox: fresh Playwright context with a non-demo sentinel; enter /?demo=1, reset, leave, and inspect storage and every request

claim: The configuration builder creates token environment-variable names but has no token field and sends no requests away from the site.
sandbox: fresh Playwright context; edit every configuration control and inspect generated text, controls, and requests

claim: The website has no analytics or advertising requests.
sandbox: fresh Playwright context; visit every page, enter demo, use the builder, and reject any cross-origin request

claim: forge-sync can create private target repositories through Forgejo, Codeberg, and GitLab API contracts.
where: landing first screen, configuration builder, README
sandbox: shipped sample repository against local Forgejo, Codeberg, and GitLab HTTP contract servers

claim: forge-sync mirrors Git branches and tags.
sandbox: fresh temporary local source and target bare Git repositories with one branch and one tag

claim: A dry run does not write target data, local state, audit data, or an archive, and a following real run creates the planned records.
sandbox: fresh local Git repositories and source/target HTTP mocks; compare dry-run and real-run requests and files

claim: forge-sync doctor checks source and target identities without writing local or remote data.
where: CLI help and README quick start
sandbox: fresh temporary configuration and local source/target HTTP servers; allow only GET identity requests and assert no state or archive path is created

claim: forge-sync is free under the MIT License.
sandbox: read the shipped LICENSE and Cargo package metadata

claim: The sample and configuration builder work offline after a first visit.
where: landing fact and offline status banner
sandbox: fresh Playwright context; visit demo online, wait for the service worker, reload offline, and edit the configuration

claim: A configured mirror run writes local state and a JSON archive alongside the target copy.
sandbox: configured local GitHub and Forgejo-compatible fixture with two repositories; inspect the selected SQLite and archive paths

claim: forge-sync daemon makes continuous configured synchronization passes.
sandbox: configured local GitHub and Forgejo-compatible fixture; run the real daemon at a one-second interval and observe two discovery passes

claim: A configured run records repository discovery, branches, tags, labels, milestones, and issues.
sandbox: configured two-repository local fixture with real Git refs and metadata API records; inspect target requests and archive files

claim: A configured run copies pull-request descriptions, reviews, inline comments, and discussion comments into a labeled target issue.
sandbox: configured local fixture with a pull request and all three comment forms; inspect target label and issue/comment requests

claim: Copied bodies retain the author, time, and original GitHub link.
sandbox: configured local fixture; inspect the rendered target issue and comment bodies for author links, timestamps, and source URLs

claim: A configured run writes JSON snapshots and commits them to a local Git archive when git_archive is enabled.
sandbox: two configured local runs with git_archive enabled and disabled; inspect JSON output and Git repository presence
